newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends down on exports, meal up on sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends down on exports, meal up on sales.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed lower on slack exports and soymeal closed higher on active exports, traders said.
"The bean complex reflected the strong demand fundamentals," a trader said. "Oil slipped a little but there is good user buying seen when oil breaks to near 23 cents."
CBOT January soyoil closed at 23.32 cents per lb, down 0.08 cent per lb.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soyoil during the week ended December 12 totaled 4,300 tonnes, below expectations for 10,000 to 20,000 tonnes.
Soymeal net exports were at 217,700 tonnes, above expectations for 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes.
Positioning was noted before the expiration of the Dec contracts at 1201 CST Thursday, the traders said.

There were some prospects for a potential explosive expiration of the December soymeal contract but it turned out to be quiet with Dec ending down $4.10 per ton at $240.90. Dec oil expired down 0.16 at 23.08.
Soyoil closed 0.05 to 0.15 cent per lb lower, with January down 0.08 at 23.32. Soymeal closed $0.70 to $2.00 per ton higher, with January up $2.00 at $230.10.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 19,000 contracts, below the 29,263 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 23,000 contracts, below 37,696 traded Wednesday.
